title: Graphs, layouts and automata
summary: Represent nodes and edges, arrange their layout, and animate graph and automata behavior.

blocks.text: Graph extends VGroup and stores nodes by ID in a Map, with an ordered edge array. addNode takes an ID string and options; addEdge takes source/target ID strings and options. Missing nodes cause edge creation to throw. GraphNode and GraphEdge are composites with configurable labels, colors and directed geometry.
Follow the [finite automaton walkthrough](/automata-walkthrough) to build a machine, inspect its trace and animate it.

Layouts includes circular, layered, bipartite and force-directed arrangements. applyLayout positions nodes immediately; morphToLayout animates positions while updating edges. updateAllEdges reconciles connectors after manual changes. Force-directed layout is a coordinate solver; it is not the same subsystem as rigid-body physics.

Seed force-layout randomness when comparing runs. A graph visualization does not implement a traversal algorithm by itself: compute BFS/Dijkstra or another algorithm in application code, then pass the resulting path/states to highlighting helpers.

Automaton builds on Graph with start/accepting states and symbol-labeled transitions. addState/addTransition construct it; trace returns a simulation result and accepts returns a boolean. Tape visualizes symbols and a moving head. AutomatonRunner sequences visual steps and verdict displays.

The current Automaton models deterministic transition lookup. A Tape visual and an automaton runner do not by themselves provide a complete programmable Turing machine. Runner step-duration arguments use seconds in the current implementation; confirm units when combining them with millisecond Scene.play timing.
Three nodes and two directed edges form one readable graph.
